transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-09 11:00am PT | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sara Patel (Nimbus Head of ML), Marcus Reed (Platform Eng), Olivia Gomez (Security)

[00:00] Liam Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros — I'm Liam, AE at Redwood, and Priya is our SE.
[00:08] Priya Nair: Hi! I'll be doing the walkthrough of the console and the per-route analytics.
[00:12] Sara Patel: Hi all, Sara here. We're excited to see the cost breakdown stuff — that's been a pain point for us.
[00:18] Marcus Reed: Marcus, platform. We want to understand allocation to product teams and how routing affects cost.
[00:24] Olivia Gomez: Olivia from security, I'll mostly listen for compliance/audit details.

[00:30] Priya Nair: Great. Quick agenda: console overview, usage analytics, per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, and then how that ties into routing and dedicated capacity. We'll also cover audit logs and SSO.
[00:40] Sara Patel: Sounds good. One thing up front — we run different models per product line and need per-team billing. Also, some legal wants data residency for patient data.

[01:00] Priya Nair: Understood. Start with the usage analytics page — so this is the aggregate view, you can filter by date range, model, route, and team tag. We show tokens in/out, latency percentiles, error rates, and cost bucketed by model and route.
[01:22] Marcus Reed: When you say route — is that per API route or per model version? Can we map it to microservices?
[01:28] Priya Nair: Yes both. Routes are logical mappings — e.g., /summarize-v2 or /chat/patient-assist — and you can tag them to a team or service. We also capture model version and infra (hosted vs dedicated).

[01:50] Liam Chen: I'll jump in — one of the features we emphasize is per-route cost attribution. In the dashboard you can export cost by route and then allocate to teams, or push tags to your billing system.
[02:02] Olivia Gomez: About audit logs — are these immutable and do they store full payloads? We need to know retention and redaction options.
[02:10] Priya Nair: Good q. Audit logs capture metadata, request IDs, token counts, latency, and optionally request/response hashes. We can configure full payload retention in Private deployments; hosted defaults to redacted payloads for PII. Retention configurable per account.
[02:30] Sara Patel: And encryption/KMS? We need customer-managed keys for some datasets.
[02:35] Liam Chen: Yes, Private supports KMS/HSM. Hosted can be integrated with customer-managed KMS for keys at rest. We'll share the security brief.

[03:00] [screen share starts]
[03:10] Priya Nair: Here's the Console. Top-left you see global usage graph, and down below the per-route table. Notice the cost column — this is computed from token usage x model cost profile + infra multipliers.
[03:30] Marcus Reed: How do you get the model cost profile? Are these Redwood-curated estimates or can we override?
[03:35] Priya Nair: Both: Redwood provides verified profiles for curated models; customers can supply custom cost factors for self-hosted/dedicated infra.

[04:00] Priya Nair: Walkthrough: click into a route, e.g., /clinical-summarize. This page shows token distribution, latency histogram, 95th percentile, cost per minute, and recent anomalies. There's also a breakdown by model variant so you can see if v2 is more expensive per token than v1.
[04:30] Sara Patel: Nice. Do you show batching effects? Our production service uses batching which reduces unit cost but increases tail latency sometimes.
[04:37] Priya Nair: Yes, we have a batching impact view — you can toggle to see cost with/without batching applied and see latency tradeoffs. The Optimize module will also recommend batching window sizes per route.

[05:10] Liam Chen: Customers frequently ask about canary rollouts and fallbacks — we show per-route rollout status and the Console can route to cheaper model variant automatically if latency/throughput breaches SLA.
[05:25] Marcus Reed: If that happens, is it logged so product teams can see a drop in quality?
[05:28] Priya Nair: Yep, fallback events are logged in the route history with reason codes. We also auto-tag any request that used fallback so you can measure quality regressions.

[06:00] [07:00 clip: minor cross talk]
[06:30] Olivia Gomez: For compliance, we need exportable audit logs and SSO integration. Do you do SAML/SCIM?
[06:35] Liam Chen: Yes SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning supported. We can provide session traces tied to user IDs for forensics.

[07:10] Priya Nair: Now digging into token-level cost: here you see a ledger style view — each request row shows input tokens, output tokens, model used, and cost. You can filter to a team tag to get precise chargebacks.
[07:36] Sara Patel: That ledger looks pretty granular. Can we get daily rollups automatically pushed to our billing S3 bucket?
[07:43] Priya Nair: Yes, export hooks available — S3/BigQuery/CSV exports on schedule.

[08:10] Marcus Reed: Any limitations for data residency — can we keep logs in EU region only?
[08:16] Priya Nair: For Private or Dedicated yes. Hosted has region controls per account; we can pin storage to a region but there are account-level settings. We'll need to capture exact residency requirements to advise.

[09:00] Liam Chen: On cost modeling — we showed the console cost column but we also provide a cost simulator. You can run a per-route simulation with traffic patterns and see projected monthly spend with different model choices (quantized variants, batching, caching).
[09:20] Priya Nair: Demo: I'll run a quick sim for /clinical-summarize. Selecting traffic 2000 req/hr, average tokens in 120, out 40, using m1-large. You can toggle to quantized variant q4 and see cost drop ~37% with slight latency change.
[09:50] Sara Patel: Do you support KV cache or prefix caching metrics? Because for summaries we reuse cache a lot.
[09:56] Priya Nair: Yes, the console shows cache hit rate per route and the simulator factors that into effective tokens billed.

[10:30] [10:40] Marcus Reed: What about tagging strategies? We have 30+ teams. Can we import tags from our internal service catalog?
[10:46] Priya Nair: SCIM + tagging API supports bulk tag imports. You can map routes to org units.

[11:10] Olivia Gomez: Any mention of third-party data sharing? We need strict controls around PHI — does Redwood do data processing agreements?
[11:16] Liam Chen: Yes, DPA & BAA available for health customers on Private deployments. We'll attach the legal packet.

[12:00] Priya Nair: Back to dashboards — you can create saved views per stakeholder: product sees per-route health and cost, finance sees aggregated spend by team, and infra sees queue-depth and GPU utilization.
[12:20] Sara Patel: Could you show an example finance view?
[12:24] [screen flicker] Priya Nair: Sure — finance dashboard aggregates routes by billing tag and shows burn by model family and by infra type (hosted vs dedicated). There's a forecast panel too.

[13:00] Marcus Reed: If we shift a route to Dedicated, does the Console update cost model immediately? Any cooldown?
[13:06] Priya Nair: It updates after provisioning and rollout; there's a short warm-up period where the console shows both projected and actuals.

[13:40] Sara Patel: Who has access controls? We need dept-level admins plus read-only auditors.
[13:47] Liam Chen: RBAC supports scoped roles: org admin, billing admin, route owner, read-only auditor. Roles map to SSO groups via SCIM.

[14:10] Olivia Gomez: Can we get a sample of your SOC2 attestation and pen test reports?
[14:15] Liam Chen: Absolutely — I'll share the security pack after the call.

[15:00] [15:20] Priya Nair: Quick note on anomalies — Console can alert on cost spikes per route and open a ticket or run an automated rollback. Alerts integrate with PagerDuty/Slack.
[15:35] Marcus Reed: Good — we need that.

[16:00] Priya Nair: Demo wrap: I exported a per-route CSV and opened the cost simulator results; attaching link to artifacts in the follow-up. Links: deck (https://redwood.ai/decks/console-walkthrough), cost-sim csv (https://redwood.ai/artifacts/ff-987-costsim.csv)

[16:30] Sara Patel: A few tradeoff questions — we worry about quality when using quantized models. How do you measure quality drift?
[16:38] Priya Nair: We have built-in eval hooks: run evals on production prompts and flag regressions. The Console ties eval results to routes so you can see if a variant introduced regressions.

[17:10] Liam Chen: Another common ask — can we set budget caps per route? We support soft caps with notifications and hard caps via routing to a cheaper fallback.

[18:00] Olivia Gomez: For the pilot, we'd want an NDA and BAA in place.
[18:05] Liam Chen: Noted. We'll get legal engaged after this call.

[18:30] [final recap] Liam Chen: Recap, we'll send pricing + ROI sheet, Priya will run a 48-hour per-route cost sim and share dashboard, Olivia will send security profile + requirements, then schedule pilot kickoff.
[18:50] Sara Patel: Thanks, that was helpful.
[19:00] Marcus Reed: Appreciate the time.
[19:05] Olivia Gomez: Thanks all.
[19:10] Liam Chen: Thanks everyone — talk soon.

End of transcript. Note: transcript contains minor transcription errors and occasional mis-attributions typical of automated meeting capture.
